title: Continuous-function coordinates for completed coefficient sections
statement: For a prime l and any scheme X, the completed coefficient ring sheaf [def-pur-twist-coefficient-rings] on the pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site] admits ring equivalences from its sections over each V to continuous functions from the underlying space of V to the p-adic integers. These equivalences commute with every restriction.

proof.text: Use the constant-sheaf comparison with continuous functions for discrete rings, naturally in finite reduction maps. The positive finite p-adic residue maps form a cone from the continuous p-adic coefficient sheaf to the specified finite constant tower.

The cone induces a morphism to the completion. Prove it bijective on sections: residues distinguish p-adic functions; conversely compatible continuous finite functions lift pointwise by PadicInt.ofCompatible, and continuity follows by the closed embedding of the compact p-adic integers into their finite residue product. Sectionwise limits, isomorphism reflection, and removal of ULift yield the natural ring equivalences.

proof_origin.place: finite-support stage-test and closed-pattern proof sketch
proof_origin.note: Strict substep of the parent argument. It asserts no nonzero-section detection and makes no reference to sheafified free modules.

mathlib_searches.query: Continuous p-adic functions as inverse limit of finite constant pro-etale coefficient sheaves; finite clopen interpolation and equality-pattern cover for pro-affine etale morphisms
mathlib_searches.results: AffineTransitionLimit existence and finite-type factorization results, plus unrelated perfectoid coefficient definitions; no interpolation, pattern-cover, or completed coefficient sheaf theorem.

Found PadicInt.toZModPow, ext_of_toZModPow, zmod_cast_comp_toZModPow, and compatible finite reduction interfaces. These are used for coefficient coordinates; they do not supply geometric scalar interpolation or pattern covers.

Continuous and profinite limit infrastructure, no finite pro-etale pattern cover or scalar interpolation theorem. Local Sheaf and WeilConjectures search found the existing discrete continuous coefficient comparison.
